A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IDEATOR study and contain readable main text and appendices. Equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material can be matched despite benchmark renaming and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original jailbreak effectiveness, transferability, ablation, and safety-benchmark results in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports those original experiments and adds an empirical comparison before and after applying AdaShield-S in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same VLM/diffusion pipeline, JSON prompting, iterative feedback, attacker models, and breadth-depth exploration procedure.

E1.justification: AdvBench, VAJM, and the benchmark's 3,654 samples across 12 topics and 46 subcategories remain unchanged. VLBreakBench is renamed VLJailbreakBench. The added defense experiment varies protection on existing victim models without reporting new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: FigStep, previously discussed as related work, becomes an evaluated comparator alongside MM-SafetyBench and IDEATOR in the new defense comparison, Table 6. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces a before/after AdaShield-S evaluation using ASR on MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, and InstructBLIP. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged; the added study provides little detail about its dataset, sample size, or defense configuration.

E4.justification: v4 adds a limited, preliminary robustness study testing whether IDEATOR remains effective against AdaShield-S relative to two competing attacks. Existing breadth/depth and modality ablations and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The parenthesized values in new Table 6 are absolute ASR changes, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All retained numerical tables are unchanged after matching renumbered tables. New Table 6 adds without/with-AdaShield-S results: IDEATOR scores 94→84%, 82→73%, and 88→87% on MiniGPT-4, LLaVA, and InstructBLIP, respectively, alongside FigStep and MM-SafetyBench results. These are added defense-condition results, not performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: The formalization in Section 3.2.1 and Appendix B's attack-set definitions, inclusion arguments, and independence-based ASR expression are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about automated black-box attacks, effectiveness, transferability, and the 3,654-sample benchmark evaluated on 11 VLMs. Benchmark renaming and conclusion editing do not materially alter these claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix D attributes resilience against AdaShield-S to diverse, subtle attack strategies. Its broad statement that competing attacks experience substantially larger reductions overlooks the InstructBLIP results: FigStep increases from 11% to 16%, and MM-SafetyBench decreases only from 29% to 27%. Existing interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The conclusion adds explicit GitHub code and Hugging Face benchmark access links, absent from v3. Existing model, hyperparameter, and hardware disclosures are retained; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked resources.

R1.justification: v4 adds Jailbreak in Pieces, JailbreakV, AdaShield, and Safety at Scale references. Section 2.2 expands its description of adversarial optimization to include harmful-content embedding alignment, while Section 5 acknowledges text-transfer benchmarks when explaining the benchmark's positioning.

P1.justification: v4 renames the benchmark, lightly revises related-work and conclusion passages, adds acknowledgements and Appendix D, and shifts former Appendices D–E to E–F. The overall narrative and main section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v4 adds defense Table 6, renumbers the previous Tables 6–7 as 7–8, and moves Figure 12 from PDF page 13 to page 15. Appendix text and the base-results table are repositioned; existing figure content and table structures are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: The added AdaShield-S comparison supplies useful evidence about an existing defense, and the new code/data links improve access information. These gains are limited by sparse experimental details and an overgeneralized interpretation of comparator reductions in Appendix D. With the core method and existing evidence preserved, the revision provides a modest net quality improvement.
